title: Worktree isolation for parallel agents: remove the shared index instead of briefing around it
description:
Recommended by TASK-191's full-depth review as the permanent disposition of the shared-index hazard. TASK-191 shipped the only mitigation implementable at its own scope (a briefing-text convention); this ticket removes the shared resource.

**Why the current mitigation is not the end state.** TASK-191 landed a pathspec-limited commit protocol plus a mandatory post-commit `git show --stat HEAD` verification. The reviewer's assessment, which I accept: it is worth shipping, it demonstrably caught the live incident, and it is *a convention backed by a second convention, with no sensor on either behaviour.* Three residual gaps, all verified against real git in a scratchpad repo during that review:

1. **Compliance-dependent.** Nothing enforces that an agent uses the pathspec form. An agent that reverts to `git add` + `git commit` reproduces the original hazard exactly.
2. **Same-path collisions are invisible.** A pathspec commit records the WORKING-TREE content of the named paths. If a sibling edits the same file concurrently, that edit is silently committed — and `git show --stat HEAD` cannot detect it, because the file list still matches intent. The backstop is blind to this class by construction.
3. **Nothing verifies the verification.** The post-commit check is itself advisory; an agent that forgets both instructions is caught by nothing.

**Why worktree isolation is the real fix.** It removes the shared index rather than coordinating access to it. The `Agent` tool already supports `isolation: 'worktree'`, giving each agent its own checkout — so the primitive exists; what does not exist is the merge/handback machinery for commits made inside a worktree. TASK-191 rejected this option **correctly for its own scope** (building that machinery is code, and that ticket was doc-only), but the reviewer was explicit that the rejection is not sound as a permanent disposition.

**The hazard is live, not theoretical.** It fired once today (an 11-file commit from two agents that had each staged only their own files, caught by post-commit inspection and repaired), and the TASK-191 developer observed siblings landing and reverting files in the shared tree in real time while implementing the ticket about it.

**Decide, do not assume.** Worktree isolation is the reviewer's recommendation, but enforced commit serialization is a legitimate alternative (`src/session-lock.js` already exists) — though note the reviewer's caveat that an advisory lock is *also* compliance-dependent, so it is not categorically stronger than what TASK-191 already shipped. A `pre-commit` hook backstop is a third option the TASK-191 developer raised. Evaluate against the three residual gaps above, not against convenience.

**Cost is a first-class input.** Worktrees cost setup time and disk per agent. Today's drive ran up to four concurrent agents; the design should say when isolation is warranted (concurrent writers) versus wasteful (a single agent, or read-only reviewers, which share the tree harmlessly today).
acceptance_criteria: The chosen approach is decided and recorded with reasoning, assessed explicitly against all three residual gaps TASK-191 leaves open (compliance-dependence, same-path invisibility, unverified verification) — state which gaps the choice closes and which it does not.

If worktree isolation is chosen, the merge/handback path for commits made inside a worktree is specified and implemented, not assumed: how a worktree commit reaches main, what happens on conflict, and what happens if the agent dies mid-work leaving an orphaned worktree.

The same-path collision class is addressed or explicitly risk-accepted with reasoning. This is the gap the current post-commit check is structurally blind to, so a solution that does not consider it has not improved on TASK-191.

Guidance states when isolation applies and when it does not — concurrent writers versus a single agent versus read-only reviewers (which share the tree harmlessly today). Isolation applied indiscriminately is a real cost for no benefit.

The behaviour is covered by specs that would fail if the mechanism were removed, following the precedent of tests/e2e/git-pathspec-commit-isolation.spec.js which reproduces the hazard and locks the mitigation.

TASK-191's pathspec protocol and post-commit verification are NOT removed unless the new mechanism strictly supersedes them — if both are kept, say which is the primary control and which is the backstop, in the briefing docs.
npm run test:all is green; no existing spec regresses; parity copies byte-identical for any briefing doc touched; dist rebuilt and committed if any bundled source changes.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**REQUEST-CHANGES** on FULL-depth review of `aad12db` + `88f0395`. **2 HIGH / 4 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.** Ticket returns to `in_progress`.

**Depth rubric inputs:** ~724 changed lines; new `src/` module (194 lines) + 266-line e2e spec + briefing docs in parity copies + doc-locks. Decisive factor: **the module performs a destructive operation** — `removeMergedWorktree` deletes worktrees — so a defect discards work that exists nowhere else.

## TIER ESCALATED: `tests-after` → `tdd`

Recording the reason. The rubric reserves `tdd` for *"security-sensitive logic, parsing, schema/state-schema changes, or state mutation with real edge-risk."* A function that permanently deletes committed work is state mutation with the highest edge-risk in this repo, and the review found two demonstrated paths to unrecoverable loss. The original `tests-after` assignment was defensible when this looked like glue over git; it is not defensible now that the safety machinery is the deliverable. **The fix round runs tests-first: each replayed attack becomes a failing spec with captured red-run evidence before the fix.**

## HIGH-1 — the guard fails OPEN on any git failure, on the one deletion path

`src/worktree-handback.js:175-176`. `aheadOut.status === 0 ? (parseInt(...) || 0) : 0` coerces **every** `rev-list` failure — unresolvable `branch`, renamed or deleted branch, typo'd `targetBranch` — to "0 unmerged commits", after which deletion proceeds. Proven live by attacks A4 (branch renamed after worktree creation) and A6 (typo'd `targetBranch: 'mian'`): **deletion executed despite unmerged commits.**

The docstring's claim is exactly inverted: it says the function *"refuses (throws) unless it can prove the worktree's branch is fully merged"* — when it can prove nothing, it deletes.

This is the **TASK-192 empty-result-contract defect class, instance five**, reproduced verbatim on a destructive operation, in the repo whose own CLAUDE.md documents four prior instances: *"the thing that finds work is broken and found nothing"* rendered as *"nothing needed doing."*

**Fix:** throw `E_GIT_FAILED` when `rev-list` exits non-zero, and treat a `NaN` parse as failure rather than zero. **Same pattern at line 149** in `detectOrphanedWorktrees` — lower stakes (under-reporting, not deletion) but fix it in the same pass.

## HIGH-2 — the guard checks the caller's CLAIM, never the worktree's actual state

`src/worktree-handback.js:170-193`. The function trusts the `branch` argument and never verifies that `branch` is what `worktreePath` actually has checked out — information available for free from `git worktree list --porcelain`, which this module **already parses**.

Demonstrated consequences:
- **A1** — a detached-HEAD worktree carrying a unique commit is deleted; the commit is left reachable from nothing. **Permanent loss.** This outright falsifies the docstring's "it can never discard unique work."
- **A7 / A12** — a worktree whose real branch has unmerged commits is deleted whenever any merged branch name is passed.

Since `git worktree remove` itself does not refuse (as the developer's own plant experiment established), this check is the **only** line of defense — and it is checking the wrong thing.

**Fix:** resolve the worktree's actual HEAD state; throw `E_WORKTREE_DETACHED` on a detached worktree; throw `E_WORKTREE_BRANCH_MISMATCH` when the checked-out branch differs from the `branch` argument; only then run the merged-ness check against that verified branch.

## MEDIUM

1. **`src/worktree-handback.js:90-98` — `mergeWorktreeBranch` misattributes a pre-existing parked merge and destroys it.** If the primary already has an in-progress conflicted merge parked by anything else, this function's merge fails, `git status` picks up the **pre-existing** unmerged entries, and it returns `{conflict:true, conflictedFiles}` naming files the handback branch never touched (A10 reported `base.txt` for a branch that only added `other.txt`) — sending the Orchestrator to adjudicate a phantom conflict. Worse, the fire-and-forget `git merge --abort` (result ignored, line 98) aborts the **other** merge, discarding partial conflict resolution sitting in the primary tree — a destructive side effect on state this function did not create. **Fix:** check for `MERGE_HEAD` before merging and refuse with `E_MERGE_IN_PROGRESS`; check the abort's exit status instead of discarding it.
2. **`tests/e2e/git-worktree-handback.spec.js:263-264` — the "removal succeeds" assertion is VACUOUS on Windows.** `expect(listAfter).not.toContain(wtClean)` compares the raw backslash `join()` path against `git worktree list` output, which is forward-slash on Windows (A11 confirmed: the raw path never appears even while the worktree exists). **The assertion passes whether or not the worktree was removed** — delete the final `git worktree remove` line and this test stays green on the platform this repo is developed on. This is the developer's own vacuity lesson un-applied four lines below where it was learned. The fix is already in the file: `wtCleanPosix` at line 226 — assert against that, captured before removal since realpath fails after.
3. **`src/worktree-handback.js:146` + the SKILL.md orphan paragraph — `detectOrphanedWorktrees` is blind to detached worktrees, even dirty ones.** The `if (!wt.branch) continue` runs **before** the dirty check, which needs no branch — so a crashed agent that left a dirty detached worktree (A9) is invisible to the exact function that exists to find crashed agents' leavings. The SKILL prose promises it lists *"every worktree ... carrying unmerged commits or a dirty working tree"* with no detached carve-out documented outside a source comment. **Fix:** run the dirty check for detached worktrees (report with `branch: null`), or at minimum document the exclusion in the prose.
4. **`targetBranch: 'HEAD'` — adjudicated as a DEFECT, not an acceptable punch-list item.** In mitigation: because `git worktree remove` never deletes the branch ref, a wrong-target check on a *branch-attached* worktree loses only a clean working directory — commits stay reachable (A6/A12 confirmed the ref survives), so the blast radius is not by itself silent commit loss. Against: the default silently binds a destructive guard to ambient checkout state, and — decisively — **combined with HIGH-1, a `targetBranch` that fails to resolve currently opens the guard entirely rather than tightening it.** **Fix:** make `targetBranch` explicit/required on `removeMergedWorktree`, or at minimum resolve it with `rev-parse --verify` and fail closed. It is the same lines being rewritten for HIGH-1 anyway. Keeping the `'HEAD'` default on read-only `detectOrphanedWorktrees` is fine.

## LOW

1. Gitignored untracked content is silently destroyed by removal (A2) — neither porcelain nor git's own check sees it. Arguably by design (ignored means disposable), but the unconditional "can never discard unique work" claim overreaches. Add the caveat to the docstring and SKILL prose while fixing the HIGHs.
2. New-test budget respected — the 4 e2e tests each encode a distinct AC, doc-locks follow the precedent file. No action.

## Attack battery — full results (real git, temp sandboxes)

| Attack | Outcome |
|---|---|
| A1 detached HEAD + unique commit | **DELETED — permanent loss** |
| A2 only unique content gitignored | **DELETED** (content destroyed) |
| A3 stash inside worktree | Deleted, **no loss** — `refs/stash` is shared |
| A4 branch renamed, old name passed | **DELETED despite unmerged — failed OPEN** |
| A6 typo'd `targetBranch` | **DELETED — failed OPEN** |
| A7/A12 commits on a different branch than passed | **DELETED** |
| A8 staged-only work | **REFUSED** (`E_WORKTREE_DIRTY`) ✓ |
| A9 dirty detached vs `detectOrphanedWorktrees` | **BLIND** — 0 orphans reported |
| A10 pre-existing parked merge | Phantom conflict + **destroyed the other merge** |
| A11 Windows slash direction | Spec assertion vacuous (MEDIUM-2) |

## Verified good — do not redo

- **AC5's headline demonstration is genuine, not incidental.** Spec lines 60-106: a plain no-pathspec `git commit` in worktree A while B holds staged work; `toEqual(['fileA.txt'])` is an exact-array assertion that would fail with `['fileA.txt','fileB.txt']` under a shared index, and line 99 independently confirms B's staged entry survived. Real counterfactual, mirroring the hazard spec.
- **Conflict detection is locale-safe as claimed** — `--porcelain=v1` plus the `UU|AA|DD|AU|UA|UD|DU` code regex, not stdout text.
- **Doc-locks non-vacuous** — literal-string pins against both copies of both real files, checked set non-empty, not fixture-derived.
- **AC1/AC3/AC4/AC6 coverage complete** — three-gap assessment table with serialization/hook rejection reasoning, when-to-isolate guidance for all three cases, the honest "visible, not resolved" residual, primary/backstop framing in both briefing docs.
- **Parity byte-identical**, hashed independently: `agents/developer.md` `791305fe…`, `skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md` `f49acfd5…`.
- **dist verified independently** — `worktree-handback` is referenced only by itself; none of the 8 entry points reach it. No rebuild owed.
- **The isolation choice itself is sound.** Nothing in the implementation undermines worktree-isolation-as-primary — every defect is in the safety machinery around handback and disposal, not in the design decision.

**Gate green throughout** (`test:all` 179 files / 2056 passed), which is precisely the point: green tests were not the story. The attacks were.

comments.body:
**Fix round 1 reviewed: PASS / APPROVE — 0 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM / 3 LOW.** Both prior HIGH deletion paths verified closed.

**Orchestrator ruling: taking one more small round rather than ticketing the MEDIUMs.** The reviewer recommended an immediate follow-up ticket; I am folding the work into this ticket instead. Reasons: (a) MEDIUM-1 carries a real induced-data-loss path, (b) MEDIUM-2 is a false claim in prose **introduced by this commit**, and shipping it into v0.20.0 would repeat the exact defect TASK-196 spent three rounds eliminating, and (c) both MEDIUMs and both LOWs live in the same two seams — one ~20-line round is cheaper than a full ticket lifecycle that would immediately become the next work item.

## Attack battery re-run independently against real git — every prior deletion path CLOSED

| Attack | Fixed (`0b3b327`) | Pre-fix (`f0244e1`) reproduction |
|---|---|---|
| A1 detached HEAD + unique commit | **REFUSED `E_WORKTREE_DETACHED`**, commit reachable | DELETED; sha reachable from **NOTHING** |
| A2 gitignored-only content | PROCEEDED — documented caveat (LOW-1, accepted) | PROCEEDED |
| A3 stash in worktree | PROCEEDED, stash survives (shared `refs/stash`) | same |
| A4 branch renamed post-creation | **REFUSED `E_WORKTREE_BRANCH_MISMATCH`** | DELETED despite unmerged |
| A6 typo'd `targetBranch` | **REFUSED `E_GIT_FAILED`** | DELETED despite unmerged |
| A7/A12 real branch differs from claim | **REFUSED `E_WORKTREE_BRANCH_MISMATCH`** | DELETED despite unmerged |
| A8 staged-only work | REFUSED `E_WORKTREE_DIRTY` | REFUSED (unchanged) |
| A9 dirty detached orphan | **REPORTED `branch=null, dirty=true`** | BLIND — 0 orphans |
| A10 pre-existing parked merge | **THREW `E_MERGE_IN_PROGRESS`**, parked merge survived | Phantom conflict + parked merge **destroyed** |

Each refusal is for the stated reason with the stated code, **coupling verified**: removing any one guard shifts the thrown code to a different one, which the specs assert against. The pre-fix column independently reproduces all 8 claimed red shapes — tdd discipline satisfied.

## `normalizeForCompare` — the introduced-risk probe, answered

**It cannot make two distinct worktrees compare equal on Windows.** `realpathSync.native` performs no case-folding of its own (probe: canonical `MixedCase-WT` preserved from lowercased input); it only unifies representations the filesystem itself says are the same directory — NTFS case variants, 8.3 short names, symlinks, `.`/`..` segments. Verified matching for forward-slash, trailing separators of both kinds, lowercased, dot- and dotdot-segments, and a genuine COM-derived 8.3 path. Unresolvable input falls back to string compare and **fails closed** as `E_WORKTREE_NOT_FOUND`.

## MEDIUM-1 — the `E_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED` fix over-fires, with an induced-data-loss path

`src/worktree-handback.js:206-213`. When `git merge` fails **without starting** a merge (unknown/typo'd branch; dirty primary tree — both probed against real git), no `MERGE_HEAD` exists, so the now-checked `git merge --abort` fails with "There is no merge to abort" (exit 128) and the function throws `E_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED` carrying a **false** *"may be left mid-merge; manual intervention required"* — while the repo is actually clean and the local edit intact. The pre-fix code correctly threw `E_MERGE_FAILED` for both; line 221 — whose own comment names "unknown branch, dirty target tree" as its examples — is now dead code for exactly those examples.

**Concrete harm:** a dirty-primary handback tells the operator the repo is mid-merge needing manual intervention; a `git reset --hard` recovery destroys the very uncommitted edit that caused the refusal.

**Fix:** after a failed merge, probe `MERGE_HEAD` (the same `rev-parse --verify -q MERGE_HEAD` used at line 174) **before** aborting; treat an abort failure as `E_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED` only when a merge was actually in progress; otherwise fall through to `E_MERGE_FAILED`. One spec per misrouted case.

## MEDIUM-2 — `detectOrphanedWorktrees` still fails open on its dirty leg, and this commit's new prose claims the opposite

`src/worktree-handback.js:257-258`: `dirty = dirtyOut.status === 0 && …` reads a **failed** `git status` as "not dirty". Probe: a worktree with staged unique work and a corrupted per-worktree index — a realistic crashed-agent artifact, i.e. exactly the population this function exists to find — makes `status` exit 128 → **0 orphans reported**. (`removeMergedWorktree` on the same worktree correctly refuses `E_WORKTREE_DIRTY`; the destructive path is protected.)

This is the TASK-192 empty-result class **on the sensor leg** — and this commit's own SKILL addition, *"Fails CLOSED (throws `E_GIT_FAILED`) rather than under-reporting if git itself cannot answer"*, is now doc-vs-code drift: true for the rev-list leg, false for the status leg. The module docstring at 232-233 makes the same over-broad claim.

**Fix:** treat `dirtyOut.status !== 0` as reportable, or scope both prose claims to the ahead-count check.

## LOW (fold into the same round — same seams)

1. `src/worktree-handback.js:116-118` — the unconditional backslash→slash rewrite is the one over-normalization vector on POSIX (a directory literally named `a\b` conflates with `a/b`). Gate it on `process.platform === 'win32'`; git emits forward-slash paths on Windows and no rewrite is needed on POSIX.
2. `src/worktree-handback.js:195` — `git status` swallowed via `.stdout || ''` on the conflict-detection path: a status failure during a real conflict yields empty `conflictedFiles`, mislabeling the outcome. Same seam as MEDIUM-1.
3. New-test budget clean; no action.

## Verified good — do not redo

- **Fail-closed audit passed** on every path reaching `git worktree remove`: `findWorktreeEntry` throws; `countUnmergedCommits` throws on non-zero **or NaN**; the dirty check counts `status !== 0` as dirty; the remove goes through `runGitOrThrow`. `parseWorktreeList` on malformed output degrades to no-match → `E_WORKTREE_NOT_FOUND`, fail-closed.
- **Vacuity sweep independently confirmed across all 12 tests:** zero `toThrow(regex)` or message-regex assertions, every throw-assertion keys off `err.code`, the one porcelain-text match (`'A  fileB.txt'`) is separator-free, and the negative path assertion at spec line 270 uses `wtCleanPosix` with sibling positive `toContain(wtPosix)` assertions acting as format sentinels. **The hunted third vacuous assertion was not found** — nearest candidate (spec line 427, `expect(catFileOut).toBe('')`) is decorative rather than vacuous, since the real reachability check is the throwing `git()` wrapper on line 426.
- Parity byte-identical, `7f9ad34a…`; dist unaffected; `check:calibration` clean; `test:all` 179 files / 2064 passed.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**Fix round 2 reviewed: PASS / APPROVE — 0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 4 LOW.** Both prior MEDIUMs and both LOWs verifiably fixed, spec-locked, red-reproduced; all gates green (`test:all` 179 files / 2069 passed); parity exact at `2c4352d5…`.

**Orchestrator ruling: one final micro-round — on a different rationale than the previous ones.** This is not "fix instance five." The reviewer identified the *generator* behind four consecutive rounds, and the ~10-line fix closes it rather than the instance. That is the same move that ended TASK-186's round cycle: stop patching regions, define the shape once.

## The new MEDIUM — the fail-open shape, one layer down

`src/worktree-handback.js:212-213`, with the identical shape latent at `:182-183`.

`mergeWasStarted = mergeHeadAfterFailure.status === 0` conflates three distinct outcomes. Git's actual semantics, confirmed empirically by the reviewer: `rev-parse --verify -q MERGE_HEAD` exits **1** when the ref is absent (the documented "missing" signal), **128** on a git-level error, **0** when mid-merge. The code reads everything that is not 0 as "absent."

Two consequence chains:
- **(a)** A merge genuinely starts and conflicts, the probe transiently errors → the abort is skipped, the repo is left **parked mid-merge**, and the thrown `E_MERGE_FAILED` affirmatively states it "failed for a reason other than a content conflict." An under-fire that inverts the over-fire this round fixed.
- **(b)** The round-1 up-front probe at `:182` carries the same conflation: a probe error while a merge is parked lets execution proceed, the merge fails on `MERGE_HEAD exists`, and if the post-failure probe then succeeds, the abort at `:242` **destroys the unrelated parked merge's partial resolution** — the exact A10 hazard round 1 closed, resurrected through the probe-error path.

Rated MEDIUM not HIGH: the trigger needs a transient git failure in a milliseconds-wide window, no deletion path is unguarded, and chain (a) self-reports (`E_MERGE_IN_PROGRESS` on the next call). Round 1 rated the identical consequence MEDIUM at a *deterministic* trigger.

**These two probes are the only remaining sites in the module that read a git failure as a state assertion** — every other call now throws or fails closed.

**Fix:** a shared three-valued `probeMergeHead(repoRoot, label)` → present / absent / throw `E_GIT_FAILED` on any status other than 0 or 1, used at **both** sites. Plus the module invariant stated at the top: *no `git()` result may be read as a state assertion; use `runGitOrThrow` or a three-valued probe.* A probe-error simulation is hard against real git; a unit-level lock on the helper's 128→throw arm suffices.

## The structural judgement, on the record for the wargame

Asked whether the module is structurally sound or has accreted patches wanting one coherent pass, the reviewer's answer: **"Mostly yes — the accretion lives in the comments, not the control flow — but the defect generator is still open."**

`mergeWorktreeBranch`'s routing is a single comprehensible if-block, not patch spaghetti, and the module now has a near-uniform invariant: every git invocation has an explicit failure disposition. The four-for-four pattern has **one identifiable cause — each new git call re-decides failure handling ad hoc**, and each round's fix added a call site (the abort check, then the probe) that made that decision wrong in a fresh way. The reviewer explicitly does **not** recommend a broader refactor: the deletion path, the parse layer, and the orphan detector are clean.

## LOW carried

1. `tests/e2e/git-worktree-handback.spec.js:700-716` — the POSIX `normalizeForCompare` specs **stub `process.platform` via `Object.defineProperty` rather than skipping on win32**, so they genuinely execute here. The honest option was taken. Residual: both platform specs use nonexistent paths, so only the `catch` fallback is exercised for the POSIX arm; the resolved-path POSIX arm (`return resolved`, `:123`) is untested anywhere. Structurally identical ternary — negligible, recorded.
2. `src/worktree-handback.js:120` — `normalizeForCompare` exported solely for testability; small public-surface widening, acceptable.
3. `src/worktree-handback.js:386-387` — stray double blank line. Cosmetic.
4. New-test budget clean; the MEDIUM-2 spec pre-asserts `statusProbe.status !== 0`, which guards against the disclosed EPERM wrong-reason failure mode.

## Verified good this round

- **Five-branch routing enumerated against real git** — typo'd branch, dirty primary, conflict, status-call failure, abort failure: all correct and spec-locked. Only the probe-error branch is defective.
- **No deletion-path regression**: the A1/A4/A6/A7/A12/A9/A10 battery re-run with the same codes; `removeMergedWorktree`'s dirty check at `:377-378` byte-identical to the prior round (not loosened); the diff's only `E_GIT_FAILED` changes are additions.
- **Prose now mechanism-accurate in all three places** — the "Fails CLOSED on both legs" claim matches `countUnmergedCommits` (`:90-106`) and the dirty leg (`:307`) in the module docstring and both byte-identical SKILL copies. The corrected sentence names its own prior falsehood, which is the right calibration posture.
- **tdd red reproduced independently** by restoring `ab7ff5d`'s source against the committed specs: exactly the five new tests fail, three with the verbatim hand-off messages.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**Micro-round reviewed: APPROVE — 0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.** Depth LIGHT (113 lines, refactor + one spec, deletion path zero hunks); the escalation trigger did not fire.

**The four-for-four streak ends at four.** This round introduced no defect — verified by enumerating all eight `.status` sites independently rather than trusting the developer's grep.

## Generator: closed in the code, verified

Every git invocation in the module now has an explicit failure disposition and **none folds a failure into a benign answer.** Full enumeration: `:84` throws · `:110` throws + NaN guard · `:141-142` three-valued · `:240` merge-success check routing into a always-throwing failure path · `:274` throws · `:293` throws · `:357` failure → `dirty: true` (fail-closed report; the `||` short-circuit means the undefined-`stdout` spawn-failure case never reaches `.trim()`) · `:428` failure → throws `E_WORKTREE_DIRTY`.

Spawn-failure behavior confirmed empirically: `spawnSync` returns `{status: null, error: ENOENT}`; `null` is neither 0 nor 1, so `probeMergeHead` falls through to the throw. Routing at both sites is semantically identical to the prior round for the 0/1 cases — only the error case changed, which was the intended delta.

**Vacuity plant executed as instructed:** with `probeMergeHead` present but its throw arm replaced by `return 'absent'`, the spec **fails** at `expect(thrown).not.toBeNull()`. It locks the throw arm, not merely the export's existence — which the original captured red (`expected undefined to be 'E_GIT_FAILED'`, from the export not existing yet) did not establish.

## MEDIUM — the invariant misdescribes the module it governs, in both directions

`src/worktree-handback.js:64-73`.

(a) *"Every call site in this module must therefore go through"* `runGitOrThrow` or a three-valued probe — **false for five existing sites** (`:238` merge, `:273` status, `:292` abort, `:356` and `:427` dirty checks), all of which use raw `git()` with inline fail-closed handling.

(b) The closing test — *"reads `.status === 0` (or `!== 0`) as its only disposition, with no throw for the 'neither yes nor no' case, has re-introduced this bug"* — textually **condemns `:357`**, which is round 2's deliberate MEDIUM-2 fail-closed fix, blessed as correct by the docstring at `:321-328`.

So the invariant claims a discipline the module doesn't practice, and flags a correct site as a bug. This is the same doc-vs-code drift class this ticket already hit in round 2 — now sitting in the text whose entire job is to be authoritative for the next contributor.

**Failure scenario:** a contributor notices the five counterexamples, concludes the invariant is aspirational, pattern-matches off the dirty checks instead — and writes the fail-**open** mirror (`status === 0 && stdout…`) that the invariant would no longer credibly forbid.

**Fix (comment-only, ~3 lines):** add a third sanctioned pattern — inline handling where every non-yes/no outcome folds into the **conservative** disposition (a throw, or the alarm-raising answer, never the benign one), citing the merge/abort/dirty sites — and scope the closing test with *"into the benign outcome."*

## LOW

1. `src/worktree-handback.js:143-146` — on spawn failure the `E_GIT_FAILED` message renders `(exit null): undefined` and drops the actionable `r.error` (e.g. ENOENT). Matches the pre-existing `runGitOrThrow` rendering at `:85`, so inherited convention rather than a new defect. `${r.stderr ?? r.error?.message ?? ''}` would render sanely at both sites whenever someone next touches this file. **Accepted, not fixed.**
2. New-test budget clean — one spec, encoding exactly this round's fix, plant-verified.

## The reviewer's judgement on whether this is finished or merely quiet

> *In the code: yes, verified... In the mechanism that stops the next contributor: mostly. What actually holds the line is mechanical — the fail-closed e2e locks that turn any loosened guard into a different thrown code, plus the probe spec. Those are solid. The invariant comment is the softer layer, and its current text is the weak point.*

That is why the 3-line amendment is worth taking rather than accepting: the mechanical locks hold regardless, but the invariant is what this round was *for*, and a false invariant teaches the wrong lesson to whoever reads it next.

**This is the final round on TASK-195.** The amendment is comment-only with a reviewer-specified fix; the Orchestrator will verify the corrected text against the eight enumerated sites directly rather than spawning a sixth review cycle.

comments.body:
APPROVED and closed. Six commits, four review cycles, tier escalated mid-flight.

**Final review depth: LIGHT** (113-line refactor + one spec, deletion path zero hunks; escalation trigger did not fire). Earlier rounds ran **FULL** — the first on rubric (new `src/` module performing a destructive operation), the rest on an empirical override: every round on this module had introduced a new defect, which outranks line count as a rubric input.

**Tier escalated `tests-after` → `tdd`** at the first review. The original assignment was defensible when this looked like glue over git; it stopped being defensible once the safety machinery around a function that permanently deletes committed work became the deliverable.

## AC1 — the decision, and what it closes

**Worktree isolation is the PRIMARY control for concurrent writers; TASK-191's pathspec protocol + post-commit `git show --stat HEAD` are RETAINED as the BACKSTOP.**

| Gap TASK-191 left open | Worktree isolation | Serialization | pre-commit hook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compliance-dependence | **CLOSED structurally** — no shared index exists, so even `git add -A` is safe | not closed (advisory lock is itself compliance-dependent) | partly |
| Same-path invisibility | **CLOSED** — becomes a visible merge conflict at handback | not closed (serializing *commits* ≠ serializing *edits*) | not closed |
| Unverified verification | N/A — structural | same problem | it *is* the verification |

Serialization was rejected on merit. Both controls are retained because isolation only applies when concurrent writers are actually spawned; the pathspec protocol governs every other case.

## AC2 — handback, all three cases implemented

`src/worktree-handback.js` (no new dependencies, `node:child_process` only):

1. **Reach main** — `mergeWorktreeBranch` runs `git merge --no-ff`. Merge, not rebase (which would rewrite SHAs already named in hand-off reports) and not cherry-pick (which risks silently dropping commits). Called by the Orchestrator after the spawn returns, never by the agent.
2. **On conflict** — aborts and returns `{merged:false, conflict:true, conflictedFiles}`; never resolves, never picks a side. Conflict detection uses `--porcelain=v1` unmerged codes (`UU/AA/DD/AU/UA/UD/DU`), not localized stdout text.
3. **Orphans** — `detectOrphanedWorktrees` reports, never deletes. `removeMergedWorktree` is the one disposal path and refuses unless it can prove full merge, clean tree, non-detached HEAD, and branch identity.

**AC3** — same-path collisions are made **visible, not resolved**; adjudication stays a human/Orchestrator call. **AC4** — concurrent writers isolate; single agents and read-only reviewers do not (the latter shared a tree all session with zero incident). **AC6** — primary/backstop framing in both briefing docs, byte-identical parity.

## What the reviews actually found — the reason this took four cycles

A real attack battery against real git, not a code read. **Round 1 found two demonstrated paths to permanently deleting committed work:**

- **A1** — a detached-HEAD worktree carrying a unique commit was **deleted, leaving the commit reachable from nothing.**
- **A4/A6** — the merged-ness guard **failed OPEN**: `rev-list` non-zero coerced to "0 unmerged commits", then delete. The docstring claimed it "refuses unless it can prove the branch is fully merged"; when it could prove nothing, it deleted.
- **A10** — `mergeWorktreeBranch` misattributed a pre-existing parked merge and its fire-and-forget abort **destroyed partial resolution it did not create.**

`git worktree remove` does not itself refuse in any of these cases — established by the developer's own plant — so these guards were the only defense, and two of them were checking the wrong thing.

**All demonstrably closed and independently re-verified**: A1 → `E_WORKTREE_DETACHED`; A4/A7/A12 → `E_WORKTREE_BRANCH_MISMATCH`; A6 → `E_GIT_FAILED`; A8 → `E_WORKTREE_DIRTY`; A9 → reported `branch:null, dirty:true`; A10 → `E_MERGE_IN_PROGRESS` with the parked merge surviving. Coupling verified: removing any one guard shifts the thrown code to a different one, which the specs assert against.

**`normalizeForCompare` — the risk the fix introduced, probed and cleared.** `realpathSync.native` performs no case-folding of its own; it only unifies representations the filesystem says are the same directory (NTFS case variants, 8.3 names, symlinks, dot-segments). It **cannot** make two distinct worktrees compare equal on Windows. Unresolvable input falls back to string compare and fails closed.

## The pattern worth keeping — four for four, then closed

Each of four consecutive rounds correctly fixed the previous defect **and introduced a new one**: fail-open guard → claim-not-state check → `E_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED` over-fire → probe-error conflation. The final review named the single cause: **each new git call re-decided failure handling ad hoc.**

The closing move was structural, not another patch — the same shape that ended TASK-186's round cycle. A three-valued `probeMergeHead` (`0`→present, `1`→absent, anything else→throw `E_GIT_FAILED`) used at **both** sites, plus a module invariant naming the three sanctioned shapes. **The streak ended at four**: the micro-round introduced no defect, verified by enumerating all nine `.status` sites rather than trusting a grep.

The final amendment corrected the invariant itself, which had misdescribed the module in both directions — claiming a discipline five sites didn't practice, and textually condemning a correct fail-closed site. Orchestrator verified the corrected text against every site: `:91` p1 · `:117` p3-throw · `:148/149` p2 · `:247` p3-routes-to-throw · `:281` p3-throw · `:300` p3-throw · `:364` p3-**alarm** · `:435` p3-throw. All accurate; the closing test now condemns only folding into the *benign* outcome, so `:364` is no longer wrongly flagged.

## Vacuity — three found across the ticket

1. **Developer, self-caught during planting**: `toThrow(/dirty/i)` passed with the guard disabled, because the mkdtemp path `wt-orphan-dirty-<hash>` appears verbatim in git's error text.
2. **Reviewer**: `expect(listAfter).not.toContain(wtClean)` compared a backslash `join()` path against git's forward-slash output — **passed whether or not the worktree was removed**, on the platform this repo is developed on.
3. **Reviewer, on request**: the probe spec's captured red proved only that the export was *absent*; a proper plant (function present, throw arm replaced by `return 'absent'`) confirmed it genuinely locks the throw arm.

## AC5 — the demonstration is real

Two worktrees off one baseline; each stages its own file; agent A commits with a **plain `git commit`, no pathspec at all**; asserts the commit captured only `fileA.txt` and B's staged file survived in B's own index. `toEqual(['fileA.txt'])` is an exact-array assertion that would fail with `['fileA.txt','fileB.txt']` under a shared index — a genuine counterfactual, mirroring the TASK-191 hazard spec.

## Gate

`test:all` 180 files / 2070 passed · `npm test` 83 files / 1105 passed · e2e handback 17 · doc-locks 16 · probe spec plant-verified · `test:since` non-empty at every round · `check:calibration` clean · parity byte-identical throughout · dist unaffected (`worktree-handback.js` is unreachable from all 8 bundle entry points, verified independently).

## Accepted residuals, stated rather than discovered

- Gitignored untracked content is still destroyed by removal (A2) — neither porcelain nor git's own check sees it. Documented in the docstring and SKILL prose.
- Same-path conflicts are made visible, not adjudicated.
- `(exit null): undefined` message rendering on spawn failure — inherited convention shared with `runGitOrThrow`, not a new defect.
- The resolved-path POSIX arm of `normalizeForCompare` is untested (structurally identical ternary to the tested one); the POSIX specs stub `process.platform` rather than skipping, so they do execute on Windows.

## Process finding for the record

**"Does this operation destroy anything?" belongs at tier-assignment time.** That single question would have set this ticket to `tdd` at step 1 instead of after a reviewer forced it. Recommend folding it into the tier rubric.
